nodes.title: Hook Engine

description.txt: Guards tool calls (blocks commits to main, rm -rf, etc.) AND injects additive context — phase-surface hints (ADR-070) and declarative skill context_queries (ADR-086). CONSUMES a MODEL-CONTROLLED tool-call envelope on stdin: that input is untrusted and is parsed without shell evaluation, with each contracted field type-asserted rather than coerced (ADR-156, #7164 — an array tool_input.command previously reached eval AND evaded every anchored guard). Prior description said only what hooks DO, never what they CONSUME. A PreToolUse hook also has a THIRD disposition beyond allow/deny: it may REWRITE tool_input before execution and let the call proceed (ADR-162, #7165) — grep-rewrite.sh prepends a grep() redefinition that neutralizes the ugrep shim which reached 9.5 GB RSS against a 21 kB file, leaving the command byte-identical. Bounded by a SINGLE-REWRITER invariant: updatedInput REPLACES tool_input (it does not merge), a sibling deny still wins, and permission rules match the ORIGINAL command. Additionally, in the repo-local `.claude/` hook surface only — never the shipped plugin surface — it enforces host resource control: at SessionStart it adopts the agent process tree into a memory-capped systemd transient scope (ADR-161). That surface split is scoped to resource control and must not be read as a general one: since ADR-227 (#8323) the SHIPPED plugin surface is itself a compaction-lifecycle consumer AND, for the first time, STATEFUL ACROSS EVENTS: `hooks/compaction-state.sh` writes a per-session ledger under `${TMPDIR}/soleur-compaction/` at `PreCompact` and reads it at `SessionStart:compact`. Every other hook here is a stateless single-event transformer, so this is a new property of the container rather than a new instance of an existing one. The ledger is machine-local, session-keyed, mode 0700, reaped at 7 days, and deliberately outside the user git tree — `hooks/compaction-state.sh` binds `PreCompact` and `SessionStart:compact`, so a customer install now carries hook code that runs on events the repo-local surface never handled. Because a plugin hook is global, that consumer is gated on a two-conjunct scope guard (a `plugins/soleur` directory AND a Soleur plan/spec artifact) rather than on `is-inside-work-tree`, which is true in every customer repo. Where this container runs server-side there is no per-user systemd bus, so that path declines and does nothing. HARNESS SURFACES: `.claude/hooks/` (Claude Code) and three blocking PreToolUse mirrors in `.openhands/hooks/`, which consume a different envelope over a protocol with no `ask` state — so ADR-157's posture is split by reason class there (ADR-165). Dispatch REGISTRIES are per-harness and audited (#8205, ADR-223): `.claude/settings.json` is Claude-canonical (its lowercase `^write$`/`^ask_user_question$` twins serve Grok and coincidentally cover those tools under Devin), `.devin/config.json` binds the triaged hook set on anchored Devin wire names (Claude matchers there are loaded-but-dead), `.codex/config.toml` and `.openhands/hooks.json` serve their harnesses, and `.claude/hooks/devin-dispositions.tsv` + `devin-matcher-parity.test.sh` keep the audit honest. On the `.claude` side exit 0 is the precondition for that posture at all: a non-zero exit makes Claude Code discard the hook's stdout JSON entirely (#7190). The two-harness enumeration describes where hook CODE lives; since ADR-178 (#7409) it no longer describes where its concurrency layer comes from — `lib/incidents.sh`, `lib/log-rotation.sh` and `pre-merge-rebase.sh` source the session-state lock/lease primitives from a THIRD, shipped location inside the deployed plugin root, reaching in from the repo side. Its TELEMETRY has a namespace contract (ADR-205, #7853): an emitted rule_id carrying a section prefix (hr/wg/cq/rf/pdr/cm) CLAIMS membership in the AGENTS corpus and is orphan-checked against it; one carrying no prefix is hook telemetry and is outside the corpus by construction, which replaced nine hand-maintained exemption stanzas in rule-metrics-aggregate.sh. Under test the sink is redirected at the RUNNER CHOKEPOINT — both bunfig preloads, the vitest globalSetup, the test-helpers.sh prelude and the _git_fixture_env import — never at the call site, and never by teaching this container to detect tests, because a false positive there would darken real operator telemetry.

plugins/soleur/ — skills, agents, knowledge base, AND the shared bash primitives shipped for execution on an installed user's machine (ADR-178, #7409): scripts/lib/session-state.sh is the cross-session lock/lease layer that gates worktree reaping. It lived under .claude/hooks/ until #7409, i.e. outside the subtree marketplace.json copies, so every installed user ran with that layer silently replaced by no-op stubs. What this system SHIPS is therefore not only prose for an agent to read — it includes executable concurrency primitives whose absence is unobservable to the user.

nodes.title: Cloudflare Tunnel

description.txt: Zero-trust inbound access — no exposed ports. ONE tunnel (tunnel.tf) with THREE ingress rules (deploy./ssh./registry.). DETERMINISM IS NOW STRUCTURAL, not one-connector: since #6594/PR-A all three ingress services are ORIGIN-RELATIVE (deploy. → http://10.0.1.10:9000, ssh. → ssh://10.0.1.10:22, registry. → tcp://10.0.1.30:5000), so whichever connector replica CF selects proxies to the correct origin (ADR-114 I2 discharged for all three). This — not 'localhost: means this host' — is what makes the management plane deterministic. NOT AN INVARIANT: the earlier 'exactly ONE connector, ADR-114 I1 enforced #6425' claim is FALSE in production. The server.tf web_tunnel_connector gate lives at cloud-init create-time user_data only, and hcloud_server.web carries ignore_changes=[user_data], so it never re-runs on a booted host. (Historical: web-2 booted 2026-07-13 BEFORE the gate merged 2026-07-15, so TWO connectors were live and measured; that web-2 was retired 2026-07-17 (#6538/#6463). var.web_hosts has two keys again: a fresh cattle web-2 (10.0.1.11, #6969) was born 2026-07-27 after the gate merged, so it runs no connector; it is a scheduler-less standby, web_colocate_inngest=false.) I1 is a construction-time gate presented as a runtime precondition — it governs only future fresh hosts, and that stays true after #6441: the NIC gate added there is FIRST-BOOT (runcmd is once-per-instance), so a fresh connector host now waits for its private address before registering and DEFERS rather than aborting on timeout, but no gate re-runs on a host that is already up. CF binds ingress to a TUNNEL and picks a connector per edge colo; before the origin-relative pin a SECOND connector silently made every non-fan-out route (deploy-status, inngest-liveness, infra-config WRITEs, ssh.) answer from whichever replica the caller's colo selected — #6425 (16h of false inngest-down alarms), #6594 (a false-green infra-config apply), #6416. Origin-relative ingress makes that harmless: the coin flip no longer determines correctness. Standing guard: the */15 connector census in scheduled-inngest-health.yml (vantage-independent; a response-poll is colo-sticky and proves nothing). Management plane only: app.soleur.ai does NOT traverse the tunnel (direct CF-proxied A record, dns.tf); no cloudflared on zot/git-data/inngest (ADR-096).

nodes.title: browser-snapshot credential guard

description.txt: Four controls with one predicate (ADR-213 + its 2026-09-14 addendum, #7947/#7980): (1) redact-a11y-snapshot.py rewrites credential-NAMED input values in an accessibility tree to <redacted> — name-based, because no surface serialises type=; (2) browser-snapshot-credential-guard.sh, a PreToolUse DENY on any Bash-invoked agent-browser snapshot not piped through that redactor; (3) the corpus lint's S2 rule, which now prescribes a STRUCTURAL disclosure verbatim (use the filename: + redactor + shred form first; a refusal whose text starts `refused by playwright-mcp-redact-proxy:` means THAT server's registration is wrapped — any other error, such as the server's own File access denied, does not); (4) playwright-mcp-redact-proxy.py, a single-file stdio JSON-RPC relay that importlib-loads the redactor by path, runs redact_text over the text of EVERY tools/call result by shape (two tools inline tree lines on the pinned server — browser_snapshot and browser_find), appends --snapshot-mode none to the wrapped argv so action tools write no raw page-*.yml, refuses browser_snapshot with filename and any call carrying an undocumented _meta argument (measured: _meta.json returns the tree as one escaped string the line-anchored predicate cannot see), withholds a JSON-escaped tree in any result and an error carrying data or tree-shaped text, drops server notifications and every server request but roots/list, refuses to start on any launch setting that opens a raw sink around it (--save-session, a non-JSON or saveSession/saveVideo/server/non-vision-capabilities config, --port/--host, --caps beyond vision, --output-mode file, any DEBUG value that can enable a pw: logger, DEBUG_FILE), and is fail-closed in three arms with NO kill switch (cannot load or self-test the redactor → exit 2 before spawning; cannot rewrite a result → isError text that never quotes input; dead child → non-zero exit, closed stdin → group SIGTERM then SIGKILL, signalled to the GROUP even when the direct child has already exited). SHIPS vs WIRES: the plugin SHIPS the proxy and, since #8156, WIRES it — plugins/soleur/.mcp.json registers `playwright` through it (mcp__plugin_soleur_playwright__*), alongside this repository's own .mcp.json; a customer's own registration stays wrapped only by their configuration. Residuals stay named, not closed: screenshots render a readonly credential panel in clear; browser_network_request / browser_evaluate / browser_run_code_unsafe return what they are asked for; console logs, PNGs and downloads are non-tree disk sinks; Page URL / title / dialog prose is inert to the predicate.

description.txt: Co-located stateless sticky router (in each web-host process, not a separate box) — resolves a session's owning host from the per-user worktree lease at the WS-upgrade handshake; local ⇒ serve, remote ⇒ proxy over one-way-TLS private net. Control ops are host-local (no cross-host forwarding). Lease in Postgres (ADR-068 user-sticky amendment)

Cluster of Hetzner Cloud hosts (Nomad clients, spread placement) running web app + CLI engine containers. Per-user worktrees are host-local in the ADR-068 §1 sense (they do NOT live on the shared git-data host) but they are NOT on the root NVMe — they sit on a per-host ATTACHED BLOCK VOLUME, workspacesVolume below (#6588 corrected this description, which said 'host-local NVMe' and led readers to conclude there was no volume to encrypt). At first boot a fresh host pulls the web app image from GHCR and extracts its baked bootstrap scripts + hooks.json.tmpl via docker cp (ADR-080, #5921) — a path web-1 can never take: the load-bearing reason is lifecycle{ignore_changes=[user_data]}, which means cloud-init never re-runs, so the bake reaches no live host (ADR-119 §(e)). ADR-143 (adopting, #6459) governs the return of a second web host: because cx33 was unorderable at the ADR-143 decision (2026-07-26 probe; still unorderable in hel1-dc2 on 2026-08-06, though it returned in nbg1-dc3/fsn1-dc14), web-2 returns as a fresh cattle **cpx22** (2c/4g x86, ~€19.49/mo net) — sized to web-1's MEASURED usage (~1.5 GB peak RAM / 0.48 load15 over 30d, not its over-provisioned 8g shape; ADR-143 D1) — a health-monitored standby at serving-weight 0 (NOT in the ingress rotation) until ADR-068 Phase-3 GA, since the sole-copy workspace volume lives on web-1 and a request routed to web-2 pre-flip would hit an empty workspace. TYPE REPINNED cx23 → cpx22 on 2026-07-26 (ADR-143 addendum, #6966), FORCED BY STOCK: the live probe that day (/v1/datacenters .server_types.available) found the ENTIRE cx line — cx23 as well as cx33 — and the ENTIRE cax ARM line orderable in 0 of 3 EU DCs, so the earlier 'cx23, in stock in hel1' claim recorded here is FALSE and is retired. cpx22 matches cx23 on cores and RAM exactly (2c/4g) and doubles local disk, so the D1 sizing rationale is unchanged — this was a price change (+€14.00/mo), not a resize. Read .server_types.available, never .supported (the hcloud CLI has the same trap). A fresh cpx22 CAN take the docker-cp bake path (unlike the frozen web-1). NOTE the DR gap the same probe exposes: web-1 (cx33), soleur-grok-dogfood (cx33) and soleur-registry (then cx23, repinned to cpx22 by #7309) all ran on types that were unorderable ON THAT DATE — restated 2026-08-06, when a live probe found both cx23 and cx33 AVAILABLE again in hel1-dc2, so the gap is not that these types are gone but that availability is not a property of the type and flips in either direction; each rebuild is a type decision even when the probe is green — they run fine but NONE can be COUNTED ON to rebuild on its current type (#6460) — the two cx33 hosts because cx33 is not orderable in hel1 where they run, and the registry (now cpx22) because a green probe is a moment, not a reservation. var.web_hosts now has two keys: web-2 was provisioned 2026-07-27 (#6969) and is a scheduler-less cattle standby (web_colocate_inngest=false — no inngest-server.service, no local reminders)
Conventions, learnings, ADRs, specs, plans, brainstorms, C4 diagrams (spec/model/views .c4 + the layouted model.likec4.json), the domain-model business-rules register, and the sync coverage summary

@playwright/mcp@0.0.78 (playwright-core 1.62.0-alpha), spawned by npx as a stdio JSON-RPC child — one newline-terminated JSON object per line, no Content-Length framing (measured) — driving a HEADED real Chrome (channel chrome, chromiumSandbox true, X11 forced at the env level) on the operator workstation with the persistent profile ~/.cache/playwright-mcp-profile, whose password manager autofills into pages the agent opens. An accessibility snapshot serialises the VALUE of every input, so a bare browser_snapshot on a login page or a credential panel returns the value inline in the tool result. Since #7980 the agent runtime reaches this server THROUGH the plugin's snapshotGuard component rather than directly — that relay is the trust boundary this node exists to show — and only on a registration that routes through it: this repository's .mcp.json does, and since #8156 the plugin's own plugins/soleur/.mcp.json registration does by default (mcp__plugin_soleur_playwright__*, on the dedicated soleur-playwright-mcp-profile under the XDG cache root — that registration ships NO config and no env forcing, so it runs the upstream defaults: headed, channel chrome — a launch-failure mode on hosts with no real Chrome installed); a customer's own registration does not unless they route it themselves; the hosted agent-runner registers no Playwright server (the vendored plugin tree excludes the plugin-root .mcp.json — both vendor steps rm it post-copy, so the hosted plugins:[type local] load never discovers it); the Inngest fleet's per-fire cron-ux-audit overlay runs a SEPARATE 0.0.75 copy, UNWRAPPED, with --snapshot-mode none appended directly (register PA-31 §(g)). Every behaviour cited is a dated observation of the pinned version, not an undertaking about the tool; the suite derives its fixture directory from the pin, so a bump without a re-capture reddens.

Durable trigger layer for server-side agents — cron, oneshot, and HTTP-armed reminders. Extracted to its own single-host private-net node so exactly-one-scheduler is enforced by topology, unblocking active-active web (ADR-030, ADR-100, #6178)

nodes.title: Workspace Git Data (/workspaces)

description.txt: Every user's checked-out repository. SOLE-COPY: refs/checkpoints/* is pushed by no refspec, session-sync.ts autocommits only knowledge-base/**, and signup-provisioned workspaces have no git remote at all — so ADR-068 §1's 'GitHub remains the durable rehydration source' does NOT hold here and there is no durable second copy anywhere (no upstream to rehydrate from). ENCRYPTED AT REST as of the 2026-07-23 cutover — the gap #6588/ADR-119 opened (PLAINTEXT ext4 while the published privacy policy claimed LUKS) is closed. HISTORY: an earlier 2026-07-20 cutover attempt (run 29782780158) landed /mnt/data on crypto_LUKS for ~27 minutes before its own dead-man timer silently remounted the retained plaintext volume over it (#6812) — do not cite that landing as the current state. The 2026-07-23 cutover is the one that certified: `workspaces-luks-verify` run **30040444418** reported `SOLEUR_WORKSPACES_READYZ ready=true writable=true populated=true workspace_count=8 expected=8` against `/dev/mapper/workspaces` — a mechanically measured verdict, not an assumed one (this distinction, per ADR-140, is the whole feature). web-2's instance was knowingly left plaintext (never served, empty) until its 2026-07-17 teardown (#6538/#6463). The fleet was single-host when this was written, so no plaintext member remained — but that was a statement about the fleet at the time, NOT an invariant, and it no longer holds: var.web_hosts has two keys since the cattle web-2 was born 2026-07-27 (#6969). The fresh web-2 (repinned cpx22, #6966) is born with its own per-host workspaces volume (hcloud_volume.workspaces, web-2 key) as RAW/empty PLAINTEXT, because the guest-side LUKS path for a FRESH host is the deferred #6931 work (ADR-141 D3) and the workspaces_luks attachment is web-1-bound and outside the birth fan-out (#6964). That member holds NO user data (sole copy is web-1's volume; web-2 is never routed pre-flip, dns.tf app record is web-1-only and the #6575 anti-pooling gate fail-closes), and it MUST NOT take serving weight while plaintext — re-evaluate at the ADR-068 Phase-3 GA flip

description.txt: Inngest durable queue + run-state. AOF on the persistent volume survives a host re-provision — the armed-reminder durability fix (#5450). AT REST: STILL PLAINTEXT ext4 (`hcloud_volume.inngest_redis`, `format = "ext4"` under `ignore_changes = [format]` — inngest-host.tf) — a seized/snapshot disk exposes the queue + run-state AOF, i.e. in-flight job payloads. Recorded as a ledgered exception (encryption-posture-ledger.json, tracking #6894). CORRECTED 2026-09-03 (#7695): the LUKS APPARATUS NOW EXISTS and this node previously said it did not — cloud-init-inngest.yml carries a five-arm blkid discriminator, inngest-luks-open.service reopens the mapper on every later boot, and the passphrase is minted at merge (inngest-redis-luks.tf). The apparatus is INERT: it cuts nothing by itself. The device becomes crypto_LUKS only when the gated `apply_target=inngest-volume-recut` dispatch destroys and recreates the volume raw, which two guards refuse unless the host is measured dark and the store measured empty. So the AT-REST claim above is unchanged and the ledger keeps its exception — what changed is that the mechanism is built rather than absent. EXTENDED 2026-09-18 (#6894): the route named in the previous clause — 'the device becomes crypto_LUKS only when the gated apply_target=inngest-volume-recut dispatch destroys and recreates the volume raw' — is no longer the only one, and is no longer the intended one for a POPULATED store. A second volume (hcloud_volume.inngest_redis_luks) is created and attached ALONGSIDE the live one, opened as a non-canonical staging mapper at first boot; the ADDITIVE blue-green cutover (ADR-142 amendment 2026-09-18) freezes the writers, copies the whole /mnt/data mount onto it, proves the copy byte-identical (listing + per-file sha256 + byte count + a read-only redis-check-aof), swaps the mount, and verifies on the new store — rolling back by reverse-copy if that verification fails. It is driven by its own latched Doppler flag INNGEST_LUKS_CUTOVER through op=luks-cutover / op=luks-rollback on cutover-inngest.yml (ADR-225), polled by inngest-luks-cutover.service every 30s, and the authority for which volume holds the store is the durable pointer INNGEST_LUKS_ACTIVE_VOLUME_ID rather than a signature on a device. AT REST IS STILL PLAINTEXT AS OF THIS EDIT: the apparatus and both verbs are merged and inert until an operator dispatches the cutover, which is deliberately not part of the merge. After the cutover the plaintext volume REMAINS ATTACHED as the rollback backstop (a plaintext copy of the same AOF — tracked with an expiry in #8285), and a probe row reporting /mnt/data on anything other than the encrypted volume pages via logtail_exploration_alert.inngest_luks_wrong_volume

Source control, CI/CD, issue tracking, and releases. ALSO, THROUGH the #7640 cutover (COMPLETED 2026-09-03), the HOST of the marketing/docs site and its certificate-admin plane: GitHub Pages SERVED soleur.ai + www.soleur.ai, and `PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pages` (custom-domain set/clear) plus `GET .../pages/health` WERE the endpoints cron-gh-pages-cert-reissue drove inside a DNS-only window (ADR-125) — that routine is now DISARMED, so read this clause as describing the rollback-path mechanism, not a live one. That hosting role ENDED at the cutover (ADR-194, #7640, applied 2026-09-03): the same Eleventy build is published to Cloudflare Pages and apex+www DNS was repointed, after which the GitHub Pages configuration is RETAINED BUT DNS-DETACHED AND NO LONGER REPUBLISHED. Retained deliberately — it is the rollback target — and NOT because it still serves. NOTE THE NARROWING (PR5, AC56): while the publish leg still ran, a DNS-only revert WAS the whole rollback; since PR5 retired that leg the retained content is FROZEN at the last PR4-era build, so restoring this origin now takes THREE acts (re-add the publish leg, redeploy, revert DNS) rather than one — and FOUR whenever apex-origin-probe.sh still reports SERVING-FROM-CLOUDFLARE-PAGES after the DNS revert, because the custom-domain ATTACHMENT can route independently of the record and must be reverted too (cutover runbook, `### Procedure` step 3). Do not quote the bare count without that conditional. Read the cert-admin path as DEAD ON THE LIVE SITE from that moment, in the same sense the `ghcr` node is dead on the pull path: the endpoints still answer, but eligibility requires the hostname to resolve to GitHub anycast and it no longer does, so no certificate can ever issue again and the origin cert stays expired by construction. This is why the reissue routine is DISARMED (apex-topology precondition + the daily detector cron removed) rather than left armed: post-cutover it would flip `www` to proxied=false and structurally could not restore it. Deletion of the GitHub Pages hosting config, its CNAME file and the remediation subsystem is DEFERRED, not done — see ADR-194 Addendum 2026-08-20 §2. ALSO (#8122, ADR-219): the UPSTREAM CONTENT SOURCE for every schema-conforming vendored bundle — goSprinto/compliance-skills (gdpr-gate rules) and General-Legal/legal-templates (legal-generate corpus, added here as the second upstream) — polled by cron-content-vendor-drift via the git/trees + git/blobs API against per-bundle NOTICE pins.

Any unauthenticated reader of the public jikig-ai/soleur GitHub repository. Receives whatever automation publishes into issue bodies and comments. Not a data subject relationship — a PUBLICATION surface, and the one egress in this model that cannot be retracted once written.

nodes.title: Shared git-data

description.txt: Shared bare git repos (objects/refs) over the private net; per-user worktrees stay host-local on NVMe. The git-data host holds the per-ref monotonic max generation and writer-side-CAS-rejects stale lease writes (ADR-068). BORN (ADR-149); the store is EMPTY until the LUKS cutover (#5274) flips `GIT_DATA_STORE_ENABLED` (every write path is gated on that flag, #6976). The host reports its own boot correctness off-host (#6982, ADR-149 item 1): boot-stage fatals to Sentry from a baked DSN, a `stage:boot_complete` signal, and gc faults to Better Stack. The birth route is gated MECHANICALLY by `git_data_rung2_rehearsal_gate`, which refuses unless `git-data-rung2-boot-evidence.env` attests a rung-2 boot rehearsal hash-bound to the CURRENT template (a hash-of-hashes over the cloud-init plus every `file()`-bound payload) and, since #8010, names a completed, successful `workflow_dispatch` run of the rehearsal workflow on `main` that uploaded a boot-evidence artifact and whose `head_sha` re-hashes to that evidence (resolved live through the GitHub REST API), with the Sentry cross-check verdict required in the file. CI root access for the cutover is ADR-220's (see the github -> gitDataStore edge). AT REST: the target store is PLAINTEXT ext4 (`hcloud_volume.git_data`, `format = "ext4"`, no LUKS apparatus) — a fresh `hcloud_volume.git_data_luks` cutover target is declared alongside it (git-data-luks.tf) but is not the live store (`GIT_DATA_STORE_ENABLED` gates the cutover). Ledgered exception (encryption-posture-ledger.json, tracking #6897), pending cutover. Since #8210 the LUKS mapper is reopened on EVERY boot by a systemd oneshot that fetches the passphrase from Doppler at boot (never from disk), so the store survives a reboot rather than silently vanishing at the first one

nodes.technology: Bare git repos over private net

description.txt: DNS, CDN, R2 storage, zero-trust tunnel — and, from #7640/ADR-194, the HOST of the marketing/docs site, a role it did NOT carry before. A direct-upload `cloudflare_pages_project` (soleur-docs, production_branch=main, no `source` block so the Git integration is deliberately NOT used) with soleur.ai and www.soleur.ai attached as `cloudflare_pages_domain` custom domains; deploy-docs.yml publishes `_site` to it with a version-pinned `wrangler pages deploy` AFTER the same six build gates, so the gate chain stays authoritative over what is served. The point is structural, not vendor preference: Cloudflare serving the site means there is NO ORIGIN LEG and no origin certificate, which is the entire failure class the migration deletes (the apex was GitHub-Pages-hosted behind this same proxy, and GitHub refuses to issue a cert for a proxied host). Also owns the rebuilt `www -> apex` 301, as an ACCOUNT-LEVEL Bulk Redirect on the `http_request_redirect` phase with its own Free quota — NOT a rule in `cloudflare_ruleset.seo_page_redirects`, whose 10-rule Free cap and whose Rule 10 (HTTPS upgrade + its inline ACME carve-out clause) are untouched by this work. Cloudflare documents Bulk Redirects as running IN FRONT OF a Pages project, which is what lets www stay attached to the project rather than parked on a black-hole IP. No new vendor, no new bill and no DPA change: already a sub-processor, already the zone owner.

Inbound email ingress (operator-inbox webhook, svix-verified) + transactional outbound (statutory triage notifications). Also the PUSH-FAILURE FALLBACK channel: a statutory push that reaches fewer than all devices falls back to Resend email (ADR-136, #6802). ADR-066.

PRIVATE GHCR registry (ghcr.io/jikig-ai/soleur-web-platform + soleur-inngest-bootstrap) — the ORIGINAL host pull source, now WRITE-ONLY: still dual-pushed by CI, but DEAD AS A FALLBACK since the Phase-5 retirement — the read PAT is revoked (GET api.github.com/user -> 401) and the minter is disabled (GHCR_MINTER_DISABLED=true; pull-token mint -> 403 DENIED), verified 2026-07-30 (#7071). It receives every image and can serve none TO HOSTS. Scope that precisely: since #7277 it demonstrably serves CI, which reads it under packages: read to re-materialise the zot store (ADR-169). The dead edge is host->GHCR, not GHCR itself. This is STRUCTURAL, not a lapsed chore: App installation tokens authenticate docker login but are DENIED docker pull on private repo-linked packages (ADR-088 arm-b), so no zero-touch GHCR pull credential can exist FOR A HOST — only a personal one. This is scoped to App installation tokens on hosts and must not be read as absolute: a CI job's GITHUB_TOKEN in this repo's context is a different credential class, and it is what ADR-169's restore path uses. Consequence: zot is the SOLE pull path and the CI zot mirror is now release-blocking (ADR-096 amendment 2026-07-30). Still bakes the host bootstrap scripts + hooks.json.tmpl, extracted via docker cp at first boot to keep cloud-init user_data under Hetzner's 32,768-byte cap (ADR-080, #5921).
Centralized secrets management with runtime injection

Error tracking + alerting, Sentry-as-IaC (ADR-031; apps/web-platform/infra/sentry/, auto-applied on push to main by apply-sentry-infra.yml — its `paths:` filter is the whole `infra/sentry/**` tree and the plan is FULL-ROOT since #6589, so declaring a resource applies it and DELETING one really destroys it, gated pre-merge by `sentry-destroy-required` + `[ack-destroy]`. The filter was widened from a 3-file list because the retired `-target=` allowlist had doubled as the gate for declared-but-never-applied). Org `jikigai-eu` on the EU/DE cluster. TWO distinct hostname classes: the Terraform/dashboard API is the ORG SUBDOMAIN (`https://<org>.sentry.io/api/`, see main.tf's provider block — NOT `eu.sentry.io`, whose regional host rewrites `-eu`-suffixed slugs to the literal `eu` org via an activeorg-cookie hijack, 302→401, breaking every read/write); DSN ingest is `de.sentry.io` (DE residency, Art. 30 PA8 §(e)). Holds the LARGER of the two paging surfaces: the issue alerts (issue-alerts.tf), the cron monitors (cron-monitors.tf — one per scheduled workflow, `failure_issue_threshold` opens an issue on a missed check-in) and the uptime monitors (uptime-monitors.tf). It is a no-SSH paging path — a host that never finished booting still pages through here. It is deliberately NOT the only one: `betterstack` is a SECOND-SOURCE vendor that pages independently precisely so a Sentry outage is survivable (see its own edge to founder). Do not 'consolidate' the two — the redundancy is the design.

OCI-native container registry (zot) on a dedicated Hetzner host (cpx22, 2 vCPU / 4 GB, hel1, volume-backed) on the private network (10.0.1.30:5000), behind a deny-all-public firewall — the zero-touch machine-credential registry that replaces GHCR on the pull path (ADR-096, #6122). TYPE REPINNED cx23 → cpx22 on 2026-08-06 (#7309) — FORCED BY STOCK VOLATILITY, not by sizing and not by unorderability: cx23 IS orderable in hel1-dc2 as of that day's live probe, but hel1-dc2 cx23 availability changed direction twice across twelve days, the first inside 24 hours (in stock 2026-07-15 and 2026-07-25, unavailable 2026-07-26 and 2026-08-04, available again 2026-08-06 — series and sources single-sourced at zot-registry.tf, anchor 'STOCK REALITY'), and a registry type change is a destroy-then-create with no capacity reservation on the sole pull path (ADR-169), where a failed revert needs a SECOND create. cpx22 was available at all three probes. Same 2c/4g shape, so the derived arch stays amd64 and the cap stays 3072m; +€14.00/mo, operator-accepted, and not billing until the host-replace actually runs. TYPE + CAP CORRECTED 2026-08-05 (#7282): this description named a larger 4 vCPU / 8 GB server type and a hardcoded megabyte cap literal, and BOTH were stale — the file contradicted itself, correctly listing the registry's real type in its own DR-gap enumeration above. History, kept because it explains the shape: #6288 sized it cx33 in hel1 (the plan's cx32 target does not exist as a Hetzner type; cx33 is the real 8 GB type, offered in hel1 not nbg1), then #6497/#6463 REVERTED var.registry_server_type to cx23 on 2026-07-16 and the description never followed. The cap is not a literal at all — it is DERIVED as host RAM − 1024m reserve, so on the live 4 GB type it is 3072m, and the whole point of deriving it is that it cannot disagree with the host the way a hardcoded 7168m did. The cap exists so zot's ~35 GB store boot scan cannot host-OOM restart-loop the box. PINNED IMAGE — LIVE-VERIFIED as of 2026-08-12 (this description previously read CODE-DECLARED / LIVE-PENDING; that is RETRACTED 2026-08-12 (#7455) as satisfied, not as wrong-when-written): zot-registry.tf pins v2.1.20 per arch and the LIVE host now RUNS it — the registry-host-replace fired 2026-08-12T20:54:12Z (run 31639782781) and the post-replace SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK rows report zot_image_digest=95a837a0afac, which is the v2.1.20 pin's digest. The earlier blocked-on-#7278-and-#6929 clause is likewise spent: the LUKS recut fired 2026-08-10. Merging a cloud-init change is STILL inert by the OPERATOR_APPLIED_EXCLUSION contract and still needs a provisioning event — that rule is unchanged and governs the NEXT such change (#7277 closed by PR #7290; Hetzner stock struck 2026-08-06 by #7309, which repinned this host to a type available at every recorded probe — see the ADR-096 amendment). `zot_image_digest` in SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK remains the off-host answer and is what settled this: it reads 95a837a0afac on the replacement host. Keep reading it rather than the pin whenever the two could diverge again. Pulled from the PUBLIC upstream registry at boot, never from itself (the bootstrap paradox — which is also the rollback lever, since a dark zot cannot block its own replacement). FRESHNESS OWNER: no bot manages that pin (Renovate has never run against this repo — measured 2026-08-05, zero PRs, no Dependency Dashboard; its inert config was removed in #7282). Detection is a poll step on rule-audit.yml (1st + 15th) that files one idempotent issue; enforcement is zot-image-staleness.test.sh in infra-validation; the analysis of record is zot-image.provenance.md. Before #7282 the only mechanism was a prose comment telling a human to run crane digest, and the pin sat 18 releases behind for ~18 months. The 60 GB store volume re-fills ONLY from a fresh CI dual-push — NOT from GHCR. Its previous description as a 'disposable GHCR mirror' with an 'atomic GHCR fallback' is RETRACTED 2026-07-30 (#7071): the sibling ghcr node in this same enumeration is now marked DEAD AS A FALLBACK (read PAT revoked -> 401, minter disabled -> 403 DENIED), so an emptied store leaves NO registry any host can pull from until CI re-pushes. The blobs stay reproducible, so this is a recoverability property, never a free one — every recut/replace of this volume takes production's only pull path offline for the gap. Hosts pull the SAME @sha256 digests here (crane-copy from CI preserves them); cosign verifies the zot-stored .sig offline against the unchanged pinned root. Plain-HTTP on the private net (integrity via cosign digest-pinning, not TLS). AT REST: guest-side LUKS, LIVE-VERIFIED as of 2026-09-20 (`hcloud_volume.registry` is declared RAW — no `format` — and cloud-init-registry.yml luksFormats/luksOpens it as /dev/mapper/registry, keyed by random_password.registry_luks via doppler_secret.registry_luks_key). The preceding CODE-DECLARED / LIVE-PENDING clause, which asserted the live device was unencrypted pending an unfired `registry-luks-recut` (#6929), is RETRACTED 2026-09-20 (#8386) — and it was already spent when written, since the recut fired 2026-08-10, as the pinned-image clause above this one records. What settled it is an off-host measurement rather than a job log: since #8386 the SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK heartbeat carries store_mount_src / store_backing_dev / store_mount_devid / store_expected_devid / store_luks in its trusted region, and boot b3ec6c3b (delivered by registry-host-replace run 35489418603) reads store_luks=yes with store_mount_devid == store_expected_devid == scsi-0HC_Volume_106585109 across 120 rows. encryption-posture-ledger.json's `hcloud_volume.registry` row therefore reads live_verification: available. Read the heartbeat, not this description, whenever the two could diverge. Scope: that measurement says the store SITS ON a LUKS container, not that the passphrase still opens it (the escrow re-test and the standing alert are #8408), and the reboot window in which zot could serve a root-fs directory is measurable but NOT yet graded. Low sensitivity (our own OCI blobs + cosign signatures, no user/repo data); integrity comes from cosign digest-pinning, not at-rest encryption (encryption-posture-ledger.json) The 60 GB store volume re-fills EITHER from a fresh CI dual-push OR, since #7277/ADR-169, from a CI-mediated GHCR restore (scripts/registry-restore-from-ghcr.sh, chained automatically after registry-luks-recut). Its earlier wording denying any GHCR refill path is RETRACTED 2026-08-05 (the literal phrase is not repeated here: AC18 is a whole-file count, and quoting it would false-fail a corrected model). Note the restore is CI-mediated and carries the REQUIRED pin set only — it is not a mirror and not a host-reachable fallback, and its authorization condition is ADR-169's rehearsed-restore gate.

The PUBLIC upstream registry (ghcr.io/project-zot/zot-linux-{amd64,arm64}) that the registry host pulls its OWN zot binary from at boot. Added 2026-08-05 (#7282): this edge was entirely unmodeled, while the sibling ghcr node — scoped to our PRIVATE ghcr.io/jikig-ai/* packages — is marked DEAD on the pull path. Reading the two as one node is what let a LIVE dependency hide behind a DEAD one. Distinct trust boundary: this is third-party code entering the sole pull path's own host, mitigated ONLY by per-arch @sha256 digest pinning plus a committed provenance analysis (zot-image.provenance.md); there is no cosign verification of the zot binary itself, unlike the app images zot then serves. No bot mutates the pin — Renovate has never run here (measured 2026-08-05).

External uptime/heartbeat monitoring (BetterStackHQ/better-uptime) AND a Logs warehouse that CI both POLLS and — since #7278/ADR-172 — WRITES TO. TWO Logs sources as of #7772, not one: 2457081 (soleur-inngest-vector-prd, eu-fsn-3) is the SHARED source the web hosts, the Inngest node and the zot registry all multiplex into with host_name as the sole discriminator; 2734275 (soleur-git-data-prd, platform http, eu-central-1a, table soleur_git_data_prd, 90d retention) belongs to git-data ALONE. The split exists because git-data is the lowest-trust host in the fleet — its `git` account serves every connected user's push — and baking the SHARED credential there meant a git-data compromise forced a rotation that darkened the web host's shipper and the registry's and cost two host replaces. Do NOT re-point local.betterstack_logs_ingest_url at the new source: that local serves the four NON-git-data consumers and moving it would put the web hosts and the registry on git-data's stream. The 'CI polls read-only' clause this description carried until 2026-08-06 is FALSE and was corrected, not softened: registry-zot-inventory.yml POSTs a SOLEUR_ZOT_INVENTORY line to the Logs INGEST endpoint using BETTERSTACK_LOGS_TOKEN read from soleur/prd, and no GitHub Actions workflow had ever POSTed here before. A CI POST bypasses Vector's VRL scrub (MOST host emitters reach this source through a Vector agent that redacts; a runner curl does not — and since #7440/ADR-184 neither does the registry host's zot-log shipper, which runs no Vector and owns its own redaction, so 'every host emitter is Vector-scrubbed' is no longer true and must not be relied on as a PII-safety inference; and in the other direction, the user-serving application container's pino WARN+ stream IS Vector-transited but its `userIdHash` is pseudonymised in the APPLICATION before egress rather than by Vector's HMAC stage, which short-circuits when the payload carries no raw userId -- so 'Vector-scrubbed' also does not mean 'Vector is what pseudonymised it', and that stream is the highest-sensitivity payload on source 2457081), so a CI-emitted marker must be PII-free BY CONSTRUCTION and is asserted so by a field allow-list test. The read direction is unchanged and is still the ONLY thing that grades a CI-emitted marker: the emitter's exit code is not evidence, so a run is green only after it reads its own run_id back out through the ClickHouse path (ADR-172 §2). Apex + inngest + registry-disk heartbeats, plus (#6438/#6548) TWO new per-host web heartbeats — web_zot_consumer (the zot-consumer serviceability probe, #6438 §1) and web_nic_guard (the §3 private-NIC-guard liveness beat, #6438 §3), both for_each var.web_hosts — and git-data, whose git_data_prd beat is FED by the web-host consumer probe (#6548) but is **deliberately NOT armed** — #6982 (D-HB) withdrew the plan to arm it, and #6548 alone now owns the decision. Three reasons, any one disqualifying: the `arm_one` call for it lives in the PER-MERGE apply job, so creating the heartbeat would make an unborn flag-off host's health a merge-blocking dependency for the whole repository; a TCP connect-and-close to :22 proves the port is OPEN, not that git transport SERVES, and sshd is up before runcmd runs — so a host whose LUKS never mounted answers on :22 and beats GREEN, installing a green light over the exact failure the interlock exists to catch; and at the time a vendor-page reading put the object pool at 10/10 (no cap is asserted any more: since #7884/ADR-222 the twice-daily heartbeat-live-reconcile prints SOLEUR_HEARTBEAT_RECONCILE_INVENTORY monitors=<n> heartbeats=<n> total=<n>, and live held 4 monitors + 9 heartbeats = 13 objects on 2026-09-15). git-data's boot correctness is instead reported HOST-SIDE by its own emitter (#6982). Registry-liveness remains paused until #6537's feeder ships and a beat is measured. All three new/newly-fed web beats (web_zot_consumer, web_nic_guard, git_data_prd) are arm-gated by the automated measure-then-arm PATCH in apply-web-platform-infra.yml (ADR-117 amendment #6438). The #5933 Item 1 per-host origin absence detector (betteruptime_monitor.web_host on web-N hostnames) is RETIRED: the origin answers only the app.soleur.ai Host, so the probe read CF 521, and betteruptime_monitor.app replaced it (uptime-alerts.tf). SINCE #7884/ADR-222 betteruptime_monitor.app_health ('soleur app database readiness', the adopted hand-made monitor 4226366) is a KEYWORD monitor on https://app.soleur.ai/health that pages when the body stops containing the compact-JSON pair supabase:connected — /health answers HTTP 200 in every database state, so the body is the only signal of a database outage. SINCE #7798/ADR-204 IT ALSO OWNS A PROPERTY SENTRY STRUCTURALLY CANNOT EXPRESS: betteruptime_monitor.soleur_www_redirect ('soleur dot ai www redirect 301', uptime-alerts.tf) asserts that https://www.soleur.ai/ returns exactly 301 WITHOUT following it (follow_redirects = false, remember_cookies = false — the vendor rejects a 3xx expectation with either enabled, HTTP 422). Sentry's uptime checker always follows 3xx and grades the FINAL response, so its predecessor sentry_uptime_monitor.soleur_www asserted `equals 301` against the apex's 200 -- an assertion it CANNOT satisfy (structural; the measurement behind it is 10/10 most recent checks failing on 2026-09-07, not a paged-back 101-day census). That monitor is now soleur_www_reachability asserting 2xx. Read the consequence rather than inferring it from the apex pattern: redirect-health is SINGLE-VENDOR. Apex reachability is deliberately second-sourced across Sentry and Better Stack, but the www 301 is watched here ALONE, because no other vendor in the stack can see the pre-redirect hop. A Better Stack outage leaves it uncovered. Detection is 180s cadence plus a 1200s confirmation window, i.e. 1380s ~23 min worst case (the cadence term is additive), which is also the real bound behind dns.tf's Camp B 'one monitor interval' acceptance — a bound that was UNBOUNDED before this, the assertion behind it having never once passed. The Logs source receives SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK + SOLEUR_PRIVATE_NIC self-reports from the deny-all registry host AND SOLEUR_PRIVATE_NIC from web-1 (the §3 web-host guard, detect+emit+alarm, NO reboot — ADR-123) and is polled from GitHub Actions via betterstack-query.sh for the zot restart-loop recurrence alarm (#6291) + follow-through soak probes — log-content recurrence alarms are in-repo GH-cron pollers, not native Better Stack alerts (ADR-096) — with ONE exception since #8097/ADR-218: Logs alerts for pure stateless per-bucket counts are Terraform-managed via BetterStackHQ/logtail, and the first, soleur-monitor-send-failed-prd, pages when a web-1 monitor unit's own Resend/Sentry send fails (the signal whose detector must survive a Sentry outage).

nodes.title: Hook Engine

description.txt: Guards tool calls (blocks commits to main, rm -rf, etc.) AND injects additive context — phase-surface hints (ADR-070) and declarative skill context_queries (ADR-086). CONSUMES a MODEL-CONTROLLED tool-call envelope on stdin: that input is untrusted and is parsed without shell evaluation, with each contracted field type-asserted rather than coerced (ADR-156, #7164 — an array tool_input.command previously reached eval AND evaded every anchored guard). Prior description said only what hooks DO, never what they CONSUME. A PreToolUse hook also has a THIRD disposition beyond allow/deny: it may REWRITE tool_input before execution and let the call proceed (ADR-162, #7165) — grep-rewrite.sh prepends a grep() redefinition that neutralizes the ugrep shim which reached 9.5 GB RSS against a 21 kB file, leaving the command byte-identical. Bounded by a SINGLE-REWRITER invariant: updatedInput REPLACES tool_input (it does not merge), a sibling deny still wins, and permission rules match the ORIGINAL command. Additionally, in the repo-local `.claude/` hook surface only — never the shipped plugin surface — it enforces host resource control: at SessionStart it adopts the agent process tree into a memory-capped systemd transient scope (ADR-161). That surface split is scoped to resource control and must not be read as a general one: since ADR-227 (#8323) the SHIPPED plugin surface is itself a compaction-lifecycle consumer AND, for the first time, STATEFUL ACROSS EVENTS: `hooks/compaction-state.sh` writes a per-session ledger under `${TMPDIR}/soleur-compaction/` at `PreCompact` and reads it at `SessionStart:compact`. Every other hook here is a stateless single-event transformer, so this is a new property of the container rather than a new instance of an existing one. The ledger is machine-local, session-keyed, mode 0700, reaped at 7 days, and deliberately outside the user git tree — `hooks/compaction-state.sh` binds `PreCompact` and `SessionStart:compact`, so a customer install now carries hook code that runs on events the repo-local surface never handled. Because a plugin hook is global, that consumer is gated on a two-conjunct scope guard (a `plugins/soleur` directory AND a Soleur plan/spec artifact) rather than on `is-inside-work-tree`, which is true in every customer repo. Where this container runs server-side there is no per-user systemd bus, so that path declines and does nothing. HARNESS SURFACES: `.claude/hooks/` (Claude Code) and three blocking PreToolUse mirrors in `.openhands/hooks/`, which consume a different envelope over a protocol with no `ask` state — so ADR-157's posture is split by reason class there (ADR-165). Dispatch REGISTRIES are per-harness and audited (#8205, ADR-223): `.claude/settings.json` is Claude-canonical (its lowercase `^write$`/`^ask_user_question$` twins serve Grok and coincidentally cover those tools under Devin), `.devin/config.json` binds the triaged hook set on anchored Devin wire names (Claude matchers there are loaded-but-dead), `.codex/config.toml` and `.openhands/hooks.json` serve their harnesses, and `.claude/hooks/devin-dispositions.tsv` + `devin-matcher-parity.test.sh` keep the audit honest. On the `.claude` side exit 0 is the precondition for that posture at all: a non-zero exit makes Claude Code discard the hook's stdout JSON entirely (#7190). The two-harness enumeration describes where hook CODE lives; since ADR-178 (#7409) it no longer describes where its concurrency layer comes from — `lib/incidents.sh`, `lib/log-rotation.sh` and `pre-merge-rebase.sh` source the session-state lock/lease primitives from a THIRD, shipped location inside the deployed plugin root, reaching in from the repo side. Its TELEMETRY has a namespace contract (ADR-205, #7853): an emitted rule_id carrying a section prefix (hr/wg/cq/rf/pdr/cm) CLAIMS membership in the AGENTS corpus and is orphan-checked against it; one carrying no prefix is hook telemetry and is outside the corpus by construction, which replaced nine hand-maintained exemption stanzas in rule-metrics-aggregate.sh. Under test the sink is redirected at the RUNNER CHOKEPOINT — both bunfig preloads, the vitest globalSetup, the test-helpers.sh prelude and the _git_fixture_env import — never at the call site, and never by teaching this container to detect tests, because a false positive there would darken real operator telemetry.

nodes.title: browser-snapshot credential guard

description.txt: Four controls with one predicate (ADR-213 + its 2026-09-14 addendum, #7947/#7980): (1) redact-a11y-snapshot.py rewrites credential-NAMED input values in an accessibility tree to <redacted> — name-based, because no surface serialises type=; (2) browser-snapshot-credential-guard.sh, a PreToolUse DENY on any Bash-invoked agent-browser snapshot not piped through that redactor; (3) the corpus lint's S2 rule, which now prescribes a STRUCTURAL disclosure verbatim (use the filename: + redactor + shred form first; a refusal whose text starts `refused by playwright-mcp-redact-proxy:` means THAT server's registration is wrapped — any other error, such as the server's own File access denied, does not); (4) playwright-mcp-redact-proxy.py, a single-file stdio JSON-RPC relay that importlib-loads the redactor by path, runs redact_text over the text of EVERY tools/call result by shape (two tools inline tree lines on the pinned server — browser_snapshot and browser_find), appends --snapshot-mode none to the wrapped argv so action tools write no raw page-*.yml, refuses browser_snapshot with filename and any call carrying an undocumented _meta argument (measured: _meta.json returns the tree as one escaped string the line-anchored predicate cannot see), withholds a JSON-escaped tree in any result and an error carrying data or tree-shaped text, drops server notifications and every server request but roots/list, refuses to start on any launch setting that opens a raw sink around it (--save-session, a non-JSON or saveSession/saveVideo/server/non-vision-capabilities config, --port/--host, --caps beyond vision, --output-mode file, any DEBUG value that can enable a pw: logger, DEBUG_FILE), and is fail-closed in three arms with NO kill switch (cannot load or self-test the redactor → exit 2 before spawning; cannot rewrite a result → isError text that never quotes input; dead child → non-zero exit, closed stdin → group SIGTERM then SIGKILL, signalled to the GROUP even when the direct child has already exited). SHIPS vs WIRES: the plugin SHIPS the proxy and, since #8156, WIRES it — plugins/soleur/.mcp.json registers `playwright` through it (mcp__plugin_soleur_playwright__*), alongside this repository's own .mcp.json; a customer's own registration stays wrapped only by their configuration. Residuals stay named, not closed: screenshots render a readonly credential panel in clear; browser_network_request / browser_evaluate / browser_run_code_unsafe return what they are asked for; console logs, PNGs and downloads are non-tree disk sinks; Page URL / title / dialog prose is inert to the predicate.

@playwright/mcp@0.0.78 (playwright-core 1.62.0-alpha), spawned by npx as a stdio JSON-RPC child — one newline-terminated JSON object per line, no Content-Length framing (measured) — driving a HEADED real Chrome (channel chrome, chromiumSandbox true, X11 forced at the env level) on the operator workstation with the persistent profile ~/.cache/playwright-mcp-profile, whose password manager autofills into pages the agent opens. An accessibility snapshot serialises the VALUE of every input, so a bare browser_snapshot on a login page or a credential panel returns the value inline in the tool result. Since #7980 the agent runtime reaches this server THROUGH the plugin's snapshotGuard component rather than directly — that relay is the trust boundary this node exists to show — and only on a registration that routes through it: this repository's .mcp.json does, and since #8156 the plugin's own plugins/soleur/.mcp.json registration does by default (mcp__plugin_soleur_playwright__*, on the dedicated soleur-playwright-mcp-profile under the XDG cache root — that registration ships NO config and no env forcing, so it runs the upstream defaults: headed, channel chrome — a launch-failure mode on hosts with no real Chrome installed); a customer's own registration does not unless they route it themselves; the hosted agent-runner registers no Playwright server (the vendored plugin tree excludes the plugin-root .mcp.json — both vendor steps rm it post-copy, so the hosted plugins:[type local] load never discovers it); the Inngest fleet's per-fire cron-ux-audit overlay runs a SEPARATE 0.0.75 copy, UNWRAPPED, with --snapshot-mode none appended directly (register PA-31 §(g)). Every behaviour cited is a dated observation of the pinned version, not an undertaking about the tool; the suite derives its fixture directory from the pin, so a bump without a re-capture reddens.

External uptime/heartbeat monitoring (BetterStackHQ/better-uptime) AND a Logs warehouse that CI both POLLS and — since #7278/ADR-172 — WRITES TO. TWO Logs sources as of #7772, not one: 2457081 (soleur-inngest-vector-prd, eu-fsn-3) is the SHARED source the web hosts, the Inngest node and the zot registry all multiplex into with host_name as the sole discriminator; 2734275 (soleur-git-data-prd, platform http, eu-central-1a, table soleur_git_data_prd, 90d retention) belongs to git-data ALONE. The split exists because git-data is the lowest-trust host in the fleet — its `git` account serves every connected user's push — and baking the SHARED credential there meant a git-data compromise forced a rotation that darkened the web host's shipper and the registry's and cost two host replaces. Do NOT re-point local.betterstack_logs_ingest_url at the new source: that local serves the four NON-git-data consumers and moving it would put the web hosts and the registry on git-data's stream. The 'CI polls read-only' clause this description carried until 2026-08-06 is FALSE and was corrected, not softened: registry-zot-inventory.yml POSTs a SOLEUR_ZOT_INVENTORY line to the Logs INGEST endpoint using BETTERSTACK_LOGS_TOKEN read from soleur/prd, and no GitHub Actions workflow had ever POSTed here before. A CI POST bypasses Vector's VRL scrub (MOST host emitters reach this source through a Vector agent that redacts; a runner curl does not — and since #7440/ADR-184 neither does the registry host's zot-log shipper, which runs no Vector and owns its own redaction, so 'every host emitter is Vector-scrubbed' is no longer true and must not be relied on as a PII-safety inference; and in the other direction, the user-serving application container's pino WARN+ stream IS Vector-transited but its `userIdHash` is pseudonymised in the APPLICATION before egress rather than by Vector's HMAC stage, which short-circuits when the payload carries no raw userId -- so 'Vector-scrubbed' also does not mean 'Vector is what pseudonymised it', and that stream is the highest-sensitivity payload on source 2457081), so a CI-emitted marker must be PII-free BY CONSTRUCTION and is asserted so by a field allow-list test. The read direction is unchanged and is still the ONLY thing that grades a CI-emitted marker: the emitter's exit code is not evidence, so a run is green only after it reads its own run_id back out through the ClickHouse path (ADR-172 §2). Apex + inngest + registry-disk heartbeats, plus (#6438/#6548) TWO new per-host web heartbeats — web_zot_consumer (the zot-consumer serviceability probe, #6438 §1) and web_nic_guard (the §3 private-NIC-guard liveness beat, #6438 §3), both for_each var.web_hosts — and git-data, whose git_data_prd beat is FED by the web-host consumer probe (#6548) but is **deliberately NOT armed** — #6982 (D-HB) withdrew the plan to arm it, and #6548 alone now owns the decision. Three reasons, any one disqualifying: the `arm_one` call for it lives in the PER-MERGE apply job, so creating the heartbeat would make an unborn flag-off host's health a merge-blocking dependency for the whole repository; a TCP connect-and-close to :22 proves the port is OPEN, not that git transport SERVES, and sshd is up before runcmd runs — so a host whose LUKS never mounted answers on :22 and beats GREEN, installing a green light over the exact failure the interlock exists to catch; and at the time a vendor-page reading put the object pool at 10/10 (no cap is asserted any more: since #7884/ADR-222 the twice-daily heartbeat-live-reconcile prints SOLEUR_HEARTBEAT_RECONCILE_INVENTORY monitors=<n> heartbeats=<n> total=<n>, and live held 4 monitors + 9 heartbeats = 13 objects on 2026-09-15). git-data's boot correctness is instead reported HOST-SIDE by its own emitter (#6982). Registry-liveness remains paused until #6537's feeder ships and a beat is measured. All three new/newly-fed web beats (web_zot_consumer, web_nic_guard, git_data_prd) are arm-gated by the automated measure-then-arm PATCH in apply-web-platform-infra.yml (ADR-117 amendment #6438). The #5933 Item 1 per-host origin absence detector (betteruptime_monitor.web_host on web-N hostnames) is RETIRED: the origin answers only the app.soleur.ai Host, so the probe read CF 521, and betteruptime_monitor.app replaced it (uptime-alerts.tf). SINCE #7884/ADR-222 betteruptime_monitor.app_health ('soleur app database readiness', the adopted hand-made monitor 4226366) is a KEYWORD monitor on https://app.soleur.ai/health that pages when the body stops containing the compact-JSON pair supabase:connected — /health answers HTTP 200 in every database state, so the body is the only signal of a database outage. SINCE #7798/ADR-204 IT ALSO OWNS A PROPERTY SENTRY STRUCTURALLY CANNOT EXPRESS: betteruptime_monitor.soleur_www_redirect ('soleur dot ai www redirect 301', uptime-alerts.tf) asserts that https://www.soleur.ai/ returns exactly 301 WITHOUT following it (follow_redirects = false, remember_cookies = false — the vendor rejects a 3xx expectation with either enabled, HTTP 422). Sentry's uptime checker always follows 3xx and grades the FINAL response, so its predecessor sentry_uptime_monitor.soleur_www asserted `equals 301` against the apex's 200 -- an assertion it CANNOT satisfy (structural; the measurement behind it is 10/10 most recent checks failing on 2026-09-07, not a paged-back 101-day census). That monitor is now soleur_www_reachability asserting 2xx. Read the consequence rather than inferring it from the apex pattern: redirect-health is SINGLE-VENDOR. Apex reachability is deliberately second-sourced across Sentry and Better Stack, but the www 301 is watched here ALONE, because no other vendor in the stack can see the pre-redirect hop. A Better Stack outage leaves it uncovered. Detection is 180s cadence plus a 1200s confirmation window, i.e. 1380s ~23 min worst case (the cadence term is additive), which is also the real bound behind dns.tf's Camp B 'one monitor interval' acceptance — a bound that was UNBOUNDED before this, the assertion behind it having never once passed. The Logs source receives SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK + SOLEUR_PRIVATE_NIC self-reports from the deny-all registry host AND SOLEUR_PRIVATE_NIC from web-1 (the §3 web-host guard, detect+emit+alarm, NO reboot — ADR-123) and is polled from GitHub Actions via betterstack-query.sh for the zot restart-loop recurrence alarm (#6291) + follow-through soak probes — log-content recurrence alarms are in-repo GH-cron pollers, not native Better Stack alerts (ADR-096) — with ONE exception since #8097/ADR-218: Logs alerts for pure stateless per-bucket counts are Terraform-managed via BetterStackHQ/logtail, and the first, soleur-monitor-send-failed-prd, pages when a web-1 monitor unit's own Resend/Sentry send fails (the signal whose detector must survive a Sentry outage).

Error tracking + alerting, Sentry-as-IaC (ADR-031; apps/web-platform/infra/sentry/, auto-applied on push to main by apply-sentry-infra.yml — its `paths:` filter is the whole `infra/sentry/**` tree and the plan is FULL-ROOT since #6589, so declaring a resource applies it and DELETING one really destroys it, gated pre-merge by `sentry-destroy-required` + `[ack-destroy]`. The filter was widened from a 3-file list because the retired `-target=` allowlist had doubled as the gate for declared-but-never-applied). Org `jikigai-eu` on the EU/DE cluster. TWO distinct hostname classes: the Terraform/dashboard API is the ORG SUBDOMAIN (`https://<org>.sentry.io/api/`, see main.tf's provider block — NOT `eu.sentry.io`, whose regional host rewrites `-eu`-suffixed slugs to the literal `eu` org via an activeorg-cookie hijack, 302→401, breaking every read/write); DSN ingest is `de.sentry.io` (DE residency, Art. 30 PA8 §(e)). Holds the LARGER of the two paging surfaces: the issue alerts (issue-alerts.tf), the cron monitors (cron-monitors.tf — one per scheduled workflow, `failure_issue_threshold` opens an issue on a missed check-in) and the uptime monitors (uptime-monitors.tf). It is a no-SSH paging path — a host that never finished booting still pages through here. It is deliberately NOT the only one: `betterstack` is a SECOND-SOURCE vendor that pages independently precisely so a Sentry outage is survivable (see its own edge to founder). Do not 'consolidate' the two — the redundancy is the design.

jikig-ai/soleur-marketplace — a public repo holding ONLY .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, README and LICENSE (~39 KB). Its single plugin entry is a keyless, unpinned git-subdir source pointing at plugins/soleur in the monorepo, so an install materialises the plugin subtree alone (~10 MiB) instead of the whole repository. Its contents are OWNED BY TERRAFORM (#7493): github_repository_file.marketplace_manifest publishes the manifest from infra/github/soleur-marketplace-manifest.json in the monorepo, so the artifact carries that repo's CI (the always-run marketplace-manifest-guard context), its required checks and the CODEOWNERS pin on /infra/github/. A default-branch ruleset requires a PR with one approval and blocks deletion and force-push, bypassed only by the org admin, the Admin repo role and the soleur-ai App. That removes the DIRECT unreviewed push path for the two other org-wide contents:write Apps (claude, entire); it does not close them — they could still collude via PR-and-approve, and the ruleset governs this repo only, so the manifest is additionally protected at apply time by a ref guard and a tree-equals-main assertion in apply-github-infra.yml. Superseded: this element previously stated it had no CI, no review and no CODEOWNERS, with scheduled-marketplace-drift.yml as its only control. Since #7490 the drift workflow carries a second job that installs the published plugin in CI and asserts delivered content (ADR-182 Decision 6).

The operator's own per-user systemd manager, reached over the D-Bus socket at /run/user/<uid>/bus (SO_PEERCRED-authenticated, same uid only, no network). Owns the cgroup v2 hierarchy for the login session: the Hook Engine asks IT to create the memory-capped transient scope each agent session runs in, so systemd stays the SINGLE WRITER to that hierarchy and no component writes cgroup directories directly (ADR-161). Units are transient and self-clean when their last process exits, so nothing is provisioned and nothing persists across a reboot.

description.txt: Source control, CI/CD, issue tracking, and releases. ALSO, THROUGH the #7640 cutover (COMPLETED 2026-09-03), the HOST of the marketing/docs site and its certificate-admin plane: GitHub Pages SERVED soleur.ai + www.soleur.ai, and `PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pages` (custom-domain set/clear) plus `GET .../pages/health` WERE the endpoints cron-gh-pages-cert-reissue drove inside a DNS-only window (ADR-125) — that routine is now DISARMED, so read this clause as describing the rollback-path mechanism, not a live one. That hosting role ENDED at the cutover (ADR-194, #7640, applied 2026-09-03): the same Eleventy build is published to Cloudflare Pages and apex+www DNS was repointed, after which the GitHub Pages configuration is RETAINED BUT DNS-DETACHED AND NO LONGER REPUBLISHED. Retained deliberately — it is the rollback target — and NOT because it still serves. NOTE THE NARROWING (PR5, AC56): while the publish leg still ran, a DNS-only revert WAS the whole rollback; since PR5 retired that leg the retained content is FROZEN at the last PR4-era build, so restoring this origin now takes THREE acts (re-add the publish leg, redeploy, revert DNS) rather than one — and FOUR whenever apex-origin-probe.sh still reports SERVING-FROM-CLOUDFLARE-PAGES after the DNS revert, because the custom-domain ATTACHMENT can route independently of the record and must be reverted too (cutover runbook, `### Procedure` step 3). Do not quote the bare count without that conditional. Read the cert-admin path as DEAD ON THE LIVE SITE from that moment, in the same sense the `ghcr` node is dead on the pull path: the endpoints still answer, but eligibility requires the hostname to resolve to GitHub anycast and it no longer does, so no certificate can ever issue again and the origin cert stays expired by construction. This is why the reissue routine is DISARMED (apex-topology precondition + the daily detector cron removed) rather than left armed: post-cutover it would flip `www` to proxied=false and structurally could not restore it. Deletion of the GitHub Pages hosting config, its CNAME file and the remediation subsystem is DEFERRED, not done — see ADR-194 Addendum 2026-08-20 §2. ALSO (#8122, ADR-219): the UPSTREAM CONTENT SOURCE for every schema-conforming vendored bundle — goSprinto/compliance-skills (gdpr-gate rules) and General-Legal/legal-templates (legal-generate corpus, added here as the second upstream) — polled by cron-content-vendor-drift via the git/trees + git/blobs API against per-bundle NOTICE pins.

An untrusted contributor opening a pull request. In CI their PR-head code executes only under pull_request isolation (fix-constraints Stage A: contents:read, no write token) and never in the privileged Stage B consumer, which opens a data-only draft follow-up PR from the default branch (ADR-074). The one PR-head artifact preflight executes on the operator's own workstation — a plan-declared discoverability probe — runs inside a bubblewrap sandbox with no credential stores bound and the repo read-only, failing closed if that sandbox cannot be established (ADR-175); its residual reach is host-loopback and outbound network (#7412). Other operator-side execution of a checked-out PR head (running its tests, its scripts, its hooks) is covered by NEITHER boundary.

SCOPE CORRECTED 2026-08-20 (#7640/ADR-194) — this CA does NOT issue the certificate the LIVE site is served with. SINCE the cutover (applied 2026-09-03) soleur.ai/www ARE served by Cloudflare Pages and terminate on the Cloudflare EDGE certificate (Google Trust Services); there is no origin leg, so no LE certificate sits anywhere on the serving path and this element must not be read as a live dependency of the apex. What survives is the RETAINED, DNS-DETACHED GitHub Pages path only, kept as the rollback TARGET — but note the narrowing that PR5 landed on 2026-09-03: a DNS-only revert WAS the whole rollback while the publish leg still ran; since PR5 retired that leg the retained content is FROZEN at the last PR4-era build, so restoring this origin takes three acts (re-add the leg, redeploy, revert DNS) and a fourth if the apex still reports SERVING-FROM-CLOUDFLARE-PAGES afterwards, because the custom-domain ATTACHMENT is then also routing. Its LE certificate: its LE certificate is expired by construction and can never re-issue (eligibility requires the hostname to resolve to GitHub anycast, which post-cutover it does not), and the remediation routine described below is DISARMED — gated on the live apex record type still being `A`, with its daily detector cron removed. Everything from here is the pre-cutover / rollback-path mechanism, unchanged and still correct for that path. ACME CA issuing the GitHub Pages custom-domain TLS cert for soleur.ai/www (ADR-125, #6657/#6698). Validation is HTTP-01 against GitHub's origin, which is why remediation must transiently flip apex+www to DNS-only — a Cloudflare-proxied record makes LE see CF anycast instead of GitHub's 185.199.x. TWO properties drive the design: (1) LE PREFERS IPv6 and retries over IPv4 only on a NETWORK-level failure of the first request (redirects get no retry), so a proxied AAAA that answers 200 with the wrong content defeats validation at any window length with no fallback — the propagation gate therefore requires AAAA ENODATA and treats a surviving AAAA as terminal, not retryable; (2) failed-validation rate limits are 5 per identifier per account per hour, refilling ~1 per 12 min with a compounding daily cap, and GitHub surfaces NONE of it — `GET /pages` returns the same `bad_authz` string whether the cause is DNS, timing, or a rate-limit pause. That invisibility is why probe-only mode (which consumes no validation attempt) is the DEFAULT for manual fires.

Source control, CI/CD, issue tracking, and releases. Any unauthenticated reader of the public jikig-ai/soleur GitHub repository. Receives whatever automation publishes into issue bodies and comments. Not a data subject relationship — a PUBLICATION surface, and the one egress in this model that cannot be retracted once written.

jikig-ai/soleur-marketplace — a public repo holding ONLY .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, README and LICENSE (~39 KB). Its single plugin entry is a keyless, unpinned git-subdir source pointing at plugins/soleur in the monorepo, so an install materialises the plugin subtree alone (~10 MiB) instead of the whole repository. Its contents are OWNED BY TERRAFORM (#7493): github_repository_file.marketplace_manifest publishes the manifest from infra/github/soleur-marketplace-manifest.json in the monorepo, so the artifact carries that repo's CI (the always-run marketplace-manifest-guard context), its required checks and the CODEOWNERS pin on /infra/github/. A default-branch ruleset requires a PR with one approval and blocks deletion and force-push, bypassed only by the org admin, the Admin repo role and the soleur-ai App. That removes the DIRECT unreviewed push path for the two other org-wide contents:write Apps (claude, entire); it does not close them — they could still collude via PR-and-approve, and the ruleset governs this repo only, so the manifest is additionally protected at apply time by a ref guard and a tree-equals-main assertion in apply-github-infra.yml. Superseded: this element previously stated it had no CI, no review and no CODEOWNERS, with scheduled-marketplace-drift.yml as its only control. Since #7490 the drift workflow carries a second job that installs the published plugin in CI and asserts delivered content (ADR-182 Decision 6).

DNS, CDN, R2 storage, zero-trust tunnel — and, from #7640/ADR-194, the HOST of the marketing/docs site, a role it did NOT carry before. A direct-upload `cloudflare_pages_project` (soleur-docs, production_branch=main, no `source` block so the Git integration is deliberately NOT used) with soleur.ai and www.soleur.ai attached as `cloudflare_pages_domain` custom domains; deploy-docs.yml publishes `_site` to it with a version-pinned `wrangler pages deploy` AFTER the same six build gates, so the gate chain stays authoritative over what is served. The point is structural, not vendor preference: Cloudflare serving the site means there is NO ORIGIN LEG and no origin certificate, which is the entire failure class the migration deletes (the apex was GitHub-Pages-hosted behind this same proxy, and GitHub refuses to issue a cert for a proxied host). Also owns the rebuilt `www -> apex` 301, as an ACCOUNT-LEVEL Bulk Redirect on the `http_request_redirect` phase with its own Free quota — NOT a rule in `cloudflare_ruleset.seo_page_redirects`, whose 10-rule Free cap and whose Rule 10 (HTTPS upgrade + its inline ACME carve-out clause) are untouched by this work. Cloudflare documents Bulk Redirects as running IN FRONT OF a Pages project, which is what lets www stay attached to the project rather than parked on a black-hole IP. No new vendor, no new bill and no DPA change: already a sub-processor, already the zone owner.
